<Rep. Nydia M. Velázquez>: Over the course of the COVID-19 pandemic, the SBA disbursed approximately $1.2 trillion of COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) and Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) funds to help small businesses adversely impacted by the crisis.\1\ In an effort to disburse PPP and COVID-19 EIDL funds swiftly, the SBA weakened and removed internal controls. Beginning in early 2021, long-standing anti-fraud controls were reinstituted and new safeguards were put into place by the Biden-Harris Administration to reduce the potential for fraud.\2\ On June 27, 2023, the SBA Office of Inspector General (OIG) issued a white paper reporting that the SBA disbursed more than $200 billion in potentially fraudulent pandemic relief.\3\ The SBA also issued a report, entitled ``Protecting the Integrity of the Pandemic Relief Programs,'' which estimates that $36 billion of the $1.2 trillion in pandemic relief was obtained fraudulently.\4\ The SBA report asserted that 86% of the likely fraud occurred in the first nine months of the pandemic,\5\ under the Trump Administration.
\1\U.S. Small Bus. Admin., Office of Inspector Gen., COVID-19 Pandemic EIDL and PPP Loan Fraud Landscape, Recommendations Update Report 25-10. (March 31, 2025).
\2\U.S. Small Bus. Admin., Office of Inspector Gen., COVID-19 Pandemic EIDL and PPP Loan Fraud Landscape, Report 23-09. (2023).
\3\Id.
\4\U.S. Small Bus. Admin., ``Protecting the Integrity of the Pandemic Relief Emergency Programs: SBA's Actions to Prevent, Detect, and Address Fraud. (June 27, 2023).
\5\Id.
As fraudsters increasingly exploited the weakened controls at the SBA and the complexity of the schemes grew, the OIG coordinated with multiple agencies. The OIG participated in DOJ COVID-19 Fraud Strike Force Teams and has 503 open investigations, as of December 30, 2025. Their work has resulted in 1,833 indictments, 1,384 arrests, and 1,193 convictions, with $1.3 billion in restitution ordered, and $1.2 billion in assets seized or forfeited.\6\
\6\U.S. Small Bus. Admin., Office of Inspector Gen., SBA OIG Congressional Newsletter, December 2025.
The OIG's ability to further combat fraud is highly dependent on the availability of budgetary resources. The FY 2026 Financial Services and General Government (FSGG) Appropriations bill provides $37 million, or level funding. It is important that the OIG have a sufficient operating budget to capitalize on two laws (P.L. 117-165 and P.L. 117-166), which extended the statute of limitations for fraud in the PPP and EIDL programs to 10 years, as well as H.R. 4495, SBA Fraud Enforcement Extension Act, which would extend the statute of limitations for the Shuttered Venues Operating Grants and the Restaurant Revitalization Fund. The single most effective action that can be taken to help the OIG recover funds is to ensure that they have adequate funding.
While the ``Put America on Commission Act 2026'' would establish a mechanism to report fraud to SBA, there are already ways for individuals to report potential fraud. They can report directly to the OIG, either through the SBA Office of Inspector General Hotline (OIG hotline) or the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee (PRAC). The SBA also has a link on their main page that will lead to a page entitled, ``Preventing Fraud and Identity Theft.'' The SBA OIG hotline has received 325,006 complaints, of which 130,338 are potentially actionable since March 2020.\7\
\7\Id.
Moreover, the qui tam in the False Claims Act allows an individual (or relator) who uncovers fraud against the government to sue in the name of the government and share the proceeds of a successful settlement. Settlements and judgements under the False Claims Act exceeded $6.8 billion in FY 2025, the highest in the history of the False Claims Act. While $5.7 billion involved the health care industry, the recoveries included some monies from the pandemic relief programs.\8\
\8\U.S. Dep't of Justice, False Claims Act Settlements and Judgments Exceed $6.8B in Fiscal Year 2025 (Jan. 16, 2026).
The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) estimated that H.R. 7129 would have increased revenues by $123 million over the 2024-2034 period. With that said, there is no authorization of appropriations to create the office or ensure it is adequately staffed. While the legislation specifies that recoveries will be used to operate the office, it could take years before those funds flow to SBA.
Nydia M. Velazquez,
Ranking Member.
